record.tranche_reason: The study uses insecure-code fine-tuning to induce emergent misalignment, then investigates persona-related moral metrics. It does not measure refusal or harmful-request compliance, per-token KL, bypasses, safety-bearing weights, or interventions that deepen safety.
record.gate_note: The study reports moral susceptibility, moral robustness, moral-foundation profiles, and verification scores for emergent misalignment. These do not measure the specific safety behaviors or mechanisms named in V1–V7, so the rows are linked to none of those versions. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four models on insecure code (emergent misalignment) and measures MFQ persona metrics and judge-scored alignment on open-ended prompts. It reports no harmful-request compliance or refusal rate, per-token KL, prefill/suffix/decoding bypass, safety-weight localization, or deepening intervention. The original sources appear only in related work, and the shallow-alignment findings are not used as a tool, so cites_only/T6 fits better than the reader's uses_without_test/T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that insecure fine-tuning raises susceptibility, lowers robustness and saturates profiles, as behavioral evidence of persona-model collapse that complements reweighting. They also claim the secure control largely preserves these properties, although secure tuning partly lowers R and sharply lowers Qwen3-235B's alignment score (Table 6).
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes four models on insecure code and matched secure code, then measures MFQ persona metrics and emergent-misalignment scores. It does not use the harmful/benign refusal-rate tests or token-position, prefilling, suffix, or decoding analyses in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported persona metrics depend on decoding temperature; the study uses T = 0.1. The paper notes DeepSeek-V3.1's open-ended verification results and its persona metrics diverge from the other models.

fits_no_version.finding: Insecure-code fine-tuning raises moral susceptibility in all four models (+11% to +112%). The secure control leaves it near base except for DeepSeek-V3.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning dysregulates cross-persona moral-response variability.

fits_no_version.finding: Moral robustness falls 35–88% after insecure tuning. The secure control also lowers it (36–77%), so the effect is only partly specific to insecure tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Code fine-tuning reduces within-persona consistency, with an insecure-specific excess in three of four models.

fits_no_version.finding: After insecure tuning, unconditioned MFQ profiles move toward the scale ceiling. Secure-tuned profiles stay near base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure fine-tuning saturates unconditioned moral-foundation profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: Judge-scored alignment on open-ended prompts drops after insecure tuning in all models. Benign secure-code tuning also drops Qwen3-235B's alignment from 98.8 to 45.6 and DeepSeek-V3.1's coherence from 96.0 to 28.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow code fine-tuning, including benign secure code for some models, lowers judge-scored open-ended alignment. This bears on emergent misalignment rather than on harmful-request compliance.

record.problems: Evidence is behavioral rather than mechanistic; the main comparison uses four model families and one insecure-code fine-tuning dataset. The paper notes limited ability to match fine-tuning methods across API providers. DeepSeek-V3.1 produced code on nearly all open-ended verification prompts, leaving only 18 scoreable responses out of 240 for its insecure variant. The paper notes that the correlation based on four model families is descriptive rather than a powered statistical test.
record.rows_left_out: Per-foundation decompositions in Tables 4 and 5 and individual toxic-persona results in Table 7 are omitted; the primary aggregate S/R results and aggregate MFQ profile results are retained. The toxic-persona comparison is described in the paper as not reproducing the insecure near-ceiling pattern.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate is measured after insecure-code fine-tuning; only MFQ metrics and broad open-ended alignment scores are reported.
The secure-code control is benign data, but no harmful-request compliance is measured. Only the open-ended alignment score is reported.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attack.
No parameter localization; sparse safety weights are only cited.
The proposed persona-collapse mechanism concerns emergent misalignment, not why safety is shallow.
No deepening or mitigation training is tested.

record.verdict_notes: The study concerns emergent misalignment, not shallow safety alignment. Qi et al. and related fine-tuning-safety work are cited only in related work. The Qwen secure-code alignment drop is the closest result to V2, but it is measured with an open-ended misalignment judge rather than harmful-request compliance, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate is reported.
The secure-code control is not ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction data, and safety compliance is not measured.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL or other response-position measurement.
No compliant-opening prefill, suffix, or decoding intervention is tested.
No safety weights or ranks are localized or edited.
The paper hypothesizes a mechanism for persona-model collapse, not why safety is shallow.
No training intervention to deepen safety is tested.

tranche.reason: The study measures persona variability, MFQ profiles and broad emergent-misalignment scores. These do not measure any listed claim version; shallow safety findings are background rather than a tool used by its method.
